about: Ukrainian official and media channels. Ukraine is a belligerent, so none of these is an
observer: an institution's own channel is graded as an interested party speaking for
itself, and the state agency and public broadcaster are marked state-aligned.
Each entry was loaded and parsed from its public preview page on 16 September 2026 and had
posted within the preceding week unless noted. Channels dropped during that check are
recorded in ``docs/TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_COVERAGE.md`` rather than guessed at here.

channels.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
channels.operator: Office of the President of Ukraine
channels.reason: The president's own channel: addresses, decrees and strike reactions, usually ahead of the presidential website.

channels.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
channels.operator: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
channels.reason: Daily operational reports and claimed Russian losses, issued by a belligerent about its own war.

channels.name: Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
channels.operator: Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
channels.reason: Missile and drone warnings and post-strike interception counts, the fastest official record of a Russian air attack.

channels.name: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
channels.operator: Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
channels.reason: Police, border and internal-security statements, including casualty figures after strikes on civilian areas.

channels.name: State Emergency Service of Ukraine
channels.reason: The rescue service's own record of fires, rubble clearance and casualties after strikes, published before official statistics.

channels.name: Ukrenergo
channels.operator: NPC Ukrenergo, the Ukrainian transmission system operator
channels.reason: Grid damage, emergency load shedding and repair status after strikes on the power system, from the operator itself.

channels.name: National Bank of Ukraine
channels.reason: Central bank decisions, reserves and wartime currency controls, issued by the authority that sets them.

channels.name: Ukrinform
channels.operator: Ukrinform, the Ukrainian state news agency
channels.reason: The state agency's wire, carrying official announcements quickly and reflecting the government's framing of them.

channels.name: Suspilne News
channels.reason: Public broadcaster newsroom with regional correspondents; state funded, with editorial independence in statute rather than in evidence.

channels.name: Ukraine NOW
channels.reason: One of the largest Ukrainian war-news channels; widely described as a government information project, which its own channel does not confirm.

channels.name: UNITED24 Media
channels.operator: UNITED24, the Ukrainian government fundraising and media platform
channels.reason: English-language output of a Ukrainian state platform whose purpose is raising support; useful and openly advocacy.

channels.name: Ukrainska Pravda
channels.reason: Long-established independent Ukrainian outlet; breaks political and procurement stories the state channels do not carry.

channels.name: NV
channels.reason: Independent Ukrainian newsroom with fast war coverage in Ukrainian and Russian.

channels.name: The Kyiv Independent
channels.reason: Independent English-language Ukrainian newsroom; the usual English entry point for Ukrainian reporting.

channels.name: Radio Svoboda
channels.operator: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, funded by the United States Congress
channels.reason: RFE/RL Russian-language service covering Ukraine and Russia; independent newsroom under US government funding.

channels.name: NEXTA
channels.operator: NEXTA, a Belarusian opposition outlet based in Poland
channels.reason: Belarusian opposition channel covering Belarus, Russia and the war; openly campaigning against both governments.
